symbols.read: Bias flips to neutral-to-bearish: price has broken below the 348.15 upper pivot to 347.15, and the combined 1D+1H read downgraded from BUY to HOLD even though the 1D direction and 1H trend remain nominally bullish. The last 1H candle (348.23→346.82) shows the pivot break in progress, and with price now under entry 348.15 and just 0.78 above the 346.37 stop, the prior "hold above 348.15" thesis is no longer valid — this is a failed pivot retest, not a pullback into support. No FVGs have opened, so 346.37 remains the sole invalidation reference; a break below it confirms the pivot failure and targets the 325.81 lower pivot, while reclaiming 348.15 would restore the bullish case toward 370.49. Regime stays NEUTRAL, so no chase either way — watch 346.37 as the line in the sand.

Bias stays bearish but the setup is closer to triggering: price has dropped from 261.35 to 249.78, breaking down out of the 258.41–263.49 bearish FVG and now sitting just above the 244.72 lower pivot, with the 1H trend flipping from up to down — a genuine change from the prior read's frozen, counter-trend bounce. The watching short (entry 244.72, stop 246.66, target 224.11) remains untriggered but is now within roughly 5 points of entry, and the combined signal still reads HOLD only because the 1D bearish and 1H bearish have not yet been confirmed by a break of the pivot. A new bear FVG at 251.05–251.58 now caps price overhead, reinforcing the bearish structure. The plan is unchanged: bias bearish below 265.34, a break of 244.72 triggers the short, and a push back above 265.34 invalidates it — the prior read is confirmed and the setup has advanced, not revised.

AVGO remains a watching sell at 326.50, still capped below the 328.58 lower pivot and far under the 380.84 upper pivot, with the 1D bearish bias and 1H downtrend both intact. The prior read's stacked FVGs have consolidated into a single bearish zone at 330.82–338.03, and the last 1H bar's -0.41% slide (326.24→324.90) replaces the earlier flat gain, confirming sellers still control the tape. The plan holds — entry 328.58, stop 332.07, target 276.32 — with a reclaim of 332.07 invalidating the short and a push above the 335.15 FVG top neutralizing the bearish structure.

Price has advanced further from 746.51 to 748.40, tightening the gap to the 751.86 upper pivot, so the bullish bias is confirmed and the BUY watch stays intact. The three layered bull FVGs at 740.32–740.93, 736.70–737.87 and 732.48–732.92 remain open and unchanged, with 740.32 still the first line to hold. The trigger is unchanged at 751.86 with entry 751.86, stop 749.86 and target 778.10, while the lower pivot has nudged up to 725.62. Invalidation remains a clean loss of 740.32, which would break the nearest supporting gap and shift focus to 736.70 and then 732.48.

BRK.B has pulled back to 543.73, essentially sitting on the 543.34 upper pivot that now acts as the line between a held breakout and a failed one — a material change from the prior read where price was 570.47 with clear air beneath it. The bias stays bullish on the intact 1D direction and 1H uptrend, but the combined signal remains HOLD and the regime NEUTRAL, so momentum still hasn't confirmed. The key development is the cluster of open bull FVGs at 542.99–544.03, 538.58–539.20, and 533.19–534.99, which now provide support shelves below price that did not exist before, while bear FVGs at 545.93–547.85 and 548.31–548.57 cap upside. Entry 543.34, stop 541.59, target 590.72; invalidation remains a push below 495.96, and a close below 542.99 would undercut the nearest bull gap and weaken the setup. Versus the prior read, the bias is confirmed but the setup has deteriorated from a comfortable hold to a pivot test, keeping this a watch rather than a chase.

Bias is bearish and the setup has firmed back from HOLD/WATCHING to an active SELL: the combined 4H+1H reading now confirms the short, revising the previous read's softened conviction back toward direction. Price at 81,800.01 is still capped below the bear FVG stack, but with open FVGs now cleared the overhead resistance is less defined, leaving 80,939.54 as the downside trigger and 84,898.00 the upper pivot. The short stays live at the 80,939.54 entry with a stop at 81,179.05 and 76,981.08 target, and the last 1H bar was a -0.11% slip (81,784.00→81,692.01), extending rather than repairing the down move. Invalidation requires reclaiming the 83,713.91 pivot and the 83,484–84,082.82 gap, with first repair at 82,647 then the 83,015–83,404 gap; the neutral regime still argues for waiting for price to reach entry rather than chasing.

Price at 2,413.98 has edged above the prior 2,402.24 and the combined 4H+1H signal has flipped back from HOLD to SELL, confirming rather than reversing the bearish bias. The 1H bounce has stalled — last bar 2,408.98→2,407.85 — and with 4H direction still bearish and 1H trend down, momentum is no longer improving. Price remains pinned between the 2,360.32 lower pivot and 2,526.62 upper pivot with no open FVGs, so the short at 2,360.32 with a 2,370.27 stop and 2,194.02 target stays valid and is now confirmed rather than on watch. A break below 2,360.32 opens the move; a reclaim of 2,526.62 invalidates. Regime stays NEUTRAL, so size accordingly until the lower pivot gives way.

Bias stays SELL and the structure is intact: price at 324.01 is still pinned below the 330.38 entry pivot with the 1H trend down, so the trade remains WATCHING, not triggered. The one change since the prior read is that the lowest bearish FVG (323.68–326.13) has been consumed and dropped from the list, leaving two overhead bearish gaps at 326.49–327.01 and 331.43–333.83; the last 1H bar eased 323.56→322.79, confirming sellers still control the near term. The plan holds unchanged: entry 330.38, stop 332.81, target 301.36. Invalidation remains a reclaim above 332.81, which would clear the top FVG and break the bearish stack.

LLY remains a BUY but the setup has weakened: price fell to 1,278.53 and the combined 1D+1H read flipped from bullish to HOLD, while the last 1H bar declined 1,282.85→1,278.38. The 1H trend is still up, but price has broken below the 1,272.33–1,275.10 and 1,275.18–1,301.46 bullish FVGs, which now sit overhead as resistance alongside a new bearish FVG at 1,284.60–1,305.15 — a clear change from the prior read, where those gaps were support beneath price. The bias stays bullish only above the 1,311.75 upper pivot, with entry, stop at 1,300.38, and target at 1,492.29 unchanged; the NEUTRAL regime still requires a confirmed reclaim before entry triggers. Invalidation is a decisive break back below 1,311.75, which reverts to a hold and exposes the 1,131.21 lower pivot, with the 1,253.48–1,260.17 bullish FVG the next support if selling continues.

META's SELL bias is confirmed and unchanged, but price has slipped to 646.01, now well below the 681.05 entry trigger — the setup is watching, not active, since the entry was never filled at this level. The 1D direction stays bearish, the 1H trend is down, and the last 1H bar fell 645.68→642.88 (-0.43%), so downside momentum is intact rather than stalled as before. The overhead bearish FVG has shifted to 648.42–650.38, now sitting just above price and acting as immediate resistance, while the 681.07–706.69 zone from the prior read is no longer the operative gap. Bias stays SELL with entry 681.05, stop 687.81, target 582.28, though the NEUTRAL regime still flags weak conviction; invalidation remains a reclaim above 687.81, which would break back into the bearish FVG structure and undercut the short.

MSFT broke down hard from 550.02 to 525.35, a decisive break below the 547.83 stop that invalidates the prior long setup and reopens the 491.22 lower pivot as the downside objective. The 1H trend has flipped from up to down while the 1D stays bullish, leaving the combined signal at HOLD and the bias now neutral-to-bearish rather than cautiously bullish. Price is sitting just above a fresh bull FVG at 523.80–523.95, the only nearby support shelf, with the 551.15 upper pivot now far overhead as reclaimed resistance. Invalidation of the bearish case is a recovery back above 547.83 and ultimately a close over 551.15; a break of the 523.80 FVG opens 491.22.

Bias is now confirmed bearish rather than a watch: price at 212.16 has broken below the 212.77 lower pivot instead of sitting pinned on it, and the combined 1D+1H regime has flipped from HOLD/NEUTRAL to SELL with the 1H trend still down. The stacked bearish FVGs at 214.17–215.09 and 215.20–220.26 remain overhead caps, though the 218.88–221.32 zone is no longer listed. The 243.37 upper pivot stays irrelevant.

Bias stays neutral-to-bearish and the setup remains a HOLD, with price at 104.95 still pinned between the 103.04 trigger and the 109.20 upper pivot. The 1H trend has flipped up since the last read while 4H direction stays bearish, so the two timeframes now conflict and the combined read stays HOLD rather than resolving into a SELL. No open FVGs remain, so overhead supply stays thin and the bear case still lacks an active zone to lean on. The SELL setup is unchanged: a break below 103.04 (entry 103.04, stop 103.51) opens 96.88, while a push through 109.20 invalidates the bear case. The only real change is the 1H trend flip from down to up, which firms the neutral stance without flipping the bias.

TSLA's bias has weakened from bullish to neutral-watch: price slipped to 372.89 and the 1H trend has flipped down, so the combined 1D+1H signal dropped from BUY to HOLD — a real change from the prior read, where the 1H was still up. The trigger remains unchanged at a close above 388.84 (stop 385.12, target 431.81), and with the FVG field still empty there is no overhead drag, but the falling 1H and the 376.41→370.34 leg argue against chasing. The 345.88 lower pivot remains the invalidation for the broader structure. Net: stand aside until a close above 388.84 confirms, and a break of 345.88 flips the structure bearish.
